title: CIVIL WAR
statement:
On June 7th, 2025, protests broke out as ICE began mass arrests in Los Angeles. The government called it a “riot,” but that implies civilian-on-civilian violence. In truth, it was state forces against the people—closer to a civil war.


In any civil war, the first weapon is voice: the government’s versus the people’s. Outnumbered, the state answers voice with guns. These clashes become postmodern rituals—casting one side as ultra-human, the other as ultra-un-human.


Observe the ritual.

title: The Quarrel
statement: This series engages with Donald Judd’s untitled concrete installations in Marfa, reinterpreting their rigid forms as vessels of contention. The spatial connection between these monolithic blocks, and the perspectives they frame enable a transference of subjectivity—allowing meaning to emerge within the abstract interplay of space and time. As Witkovsky once posits, “Looking and desiring are the very bases of abstraction.” Here, I project the dynamics of quarrel onto these structures, allowing their geometric austerity to embody conflict, negotiation, and resolution within voids of perception.
